name: Gross, process and cut tissue into slides (community surgical pathology)
summary: Biopsies taken in physicians' offices (mostly skin, gastrointestinal, prostate and gynaecologic) arrive in formalin and are checked, entered as surgical cases, grossed into labelled cassettes, processed overnight, embedded in paraffin, cut on microtomes, stained and matched to their cases before delivery to a pathologist. Histotechnologists and pathologists' assistants do skilled hand work at every stage, much of it on evening and night shifts. Overnight processing sets a one-day minimum, weekend schedules add up to two days, and most errors are labelling slips at accessioning, block labelling and cutting that the next handoff usually catches.

baseline.org_archetype: A large Canadian community laboratory company with central histology at its main laboratories, conventional overnight tissue processors and automated stainers, cutting Monday to Friday.
baseline.notes: About 13,000 surgical cases a month, mostly small biopsies of one to three blocks.

trigger: An accessioned tissue specimen with its requisition reaches the histology laboratory.
end_state: Stained slides matched to the case are delivered to the pathologist with the requisition and gross description, and the blocks are filed.

volume.seasonality: Weekday arrivals; fewer biopsies in summer and holiday weeks when offices close.

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Anatomic pathology case management with dictation and synoptic reporting
Tissue processors, embedding centres, microtomes, stainers and coverslippers
Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)
Block and slide filing and retention storage

steps.name: Check containers against requisitions
steps.description: The histology laboratory assistant unpacks the biopsy containers that arrived from processing, checks that each container carries two patient identifiers and the site, matches the containers to the requisition and LIS order, confirms formalin is present and sorts small biopsies from larger specimens.

error.defect_description: Container labelled with the wrong site or part not matched to the requisition.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

next.condition: missing or mismatched label, site or requisition

evidence.note: Matching labels to documentation is a listed duty; 20.9% of mislabelling arises before accessioning and 12.4% at accessioning. Shares and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a container or requisition discrepancy
steps.description: The laboratory assistant records the discrepancy, phones the physician's office to confirm the patient, site or number of containers, and documents the answer; irreplaceable tissue is processed on hold rather than rejected.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

next.condition: written confirmation required from the physician

evidence.note: Common practice; branch shares and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Physician's office returns a signed identification form
steps.description: The office faxes back a signed form confirming the patient and specimen details; the case continues on hold until it arrives.

evidence.note: Response times are estimates.

steps.name: Create the surgical case and print cassettes
steps.description: The laboratory assistant creates the surgical pathology case in the anatomic pathology system from the LIS order, enters each specimen part and site, and prints the labelled cassettes and part labels for grossing.

error.defect_description: Part entered against the wrong site or case.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

next.condition: small biopsy grossed by a histotechnologist

evidence.note: Data entry from requisitions is a listed duty; the share grossed by technologists is an estimate.

steps.name: Gross the specimen and submit tissue
steps.description: The pathologists' assistant confirms the identifiers against the cassettes, describes each part (size, colour, number of fragments), inks margins on excisions, sections the tissue into cassettes and dictates or types the gross description.

error.defect_description: Tissue placed in the wrong cassette, fragment lost or carried over.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): gross examination by a pathologist or a qualified delegate following written protocols

evidence.note: Grossing duties and evening and overnight shifts are described in the company postings; minutes are estimates for community biopsies.

steps.name: Gross small biopsies by protocol
steps.description: The histotechnologist counts and measures the fragments of a small biopsy, wraps or bags them, places them in the labelled cassette and records the gross description from a template.

error.defect_description: Fragment count wrong or tissue lost.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): gross examination by a qualified delegate following written protocols

evidence.note: Grossing is part of the histology MLT duties in the company posting; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Decalcify a calcified specimen
steps.description: The histotechnologist places the calcified tissue in decalcifying solution, checks it daily for the end point, then rinses and cassettes it for processing.

evidence.note: Decalcification adds 1 to 2 days; share and minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Count cassettes and load the tissue processor
steps.description: The histotechnologist reconciles the number of cassettes against the grossing log, loads the baskets into the tissue processor and starts the overnight protocol once tissue has fixed long enough in formalin.

error.defect_description: Cassette left out of the run.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

next.condition: received Friday or Saturday; held for the weekend

evidence.note: Loading processors per SOP is a listed duty and overnight fixation adds a day; the weekend share is an estimate.

steps.name: Hold cassettes over the weekend
steps.description: Cassettes from late in the week stay in formalin or on a delayed-start processor program until the Sunday night or Monday run; nobody works on them meanwhile.

evidence.note: Weekend schedules are an estimate of common practice for laboratories that cut Monday to Friday.

steps.name: Tissue processor runs the overnight schedule
steps.description: The processor moves the tissue through formalin, graded alcohols, a clearing agent and molten paraffin over about twelve hours; nobody works on the case while it runs.

evidence.note: Overnight cycles against about 3-hour short cycles are described; the 8 to 14 hour range is an estimate.

steps.name: Embed tissue in paraffin blocks
steps.description: The histotechnologist unloads the processor, checks the cassette count again, orients each fragment in a mould at the embedding centre (on edge for skin, flat for mucosal biopsies) and cools the blocks.

error.defect_description: Poor orientation or a fragment left in the cassette.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

evidence.note: Embedding is a listed duty; minutes are estimates for about two blocks a case.

steps.name: Search for a missing cassette or tissue
steps.description: The charge technologist checks the processor baskets, grossing station and logs, traces the missing cassette or fragment, and documents the event as a nonconformance if it cannot be found.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Cut sections and pick up slides
steps.description: The histotechnologist trims each block on the microtome, cuts ribbons at about 4 micrometres, floats them on the water bath and picks up the number of levels the protocol calls for onto slides labelled for that block, checking block and slide labels one block at a time.

error.defect_description: Section put on a slide labelled for another block, or poor section quality.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

evidence.note: 30.4% of mislabelling arises at tissue cutting and continuous one-by-one flow reduces cutting and labelling errors; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Stain and coverslip the slides
steps.description: The slides run through the automated haematoxylin and eosin stainer and coverslipper in racks; nobody works on the case while the instrument runs.

evidence.note: Stainer run and rack batching times are estimates.

steps.name: Match slides to blocks and check section quality
steps.description: The laboratory assistant checks every slide label against its block and the case, counts slides against the levels ordered, flags folds, holes or weak staining for the technologist, and sorts the slides by pathologist.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

evidence.note: Most mislabelling is caught in the next one or two steps; the 4.5% defect share is an estimate.

steps.name: Recut or relabel a defective slide
steps.description: The histotechnologist relabels a mislabelled slide after checking the block, or recuts a block with folded, torn or thick sections, and sends the new slide through staining.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): positive identification and reconciliation of containers, cassettes, blocks and slides at each handoff

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: File the blocks
steps.description: The laboratory assistant files the cut blocks in numbered drawers by case number for retention and later retrieval for levels, special stains or immunohistochemistry.

control.basis: ISO 15189 accredited anatomic pathology procedures (IQMH in Ontario, CAP and MANQAP in Manitoba): retention of blocks and slides so they are retrievable

evidence.note: Common practice; minutes are estimates.

steps.name: Deliver slides with requisitions to the pathologist
steps.description: The laboratory assistant assembles each case's slides with the requisition and gross description, scans the handoff in the anatomic pathology system and delivers the trays to the pathologists' offices on the scheduled runs.

evidence.note: Slide allocation and delivery is named as a delay point; delivery times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Container or requisition discrepancy
exceptions.description: Labels, sites or container counts do not match; resolved by phone or by a signed form while the tissue is held.

exceptions.name: Weekend hold
exceptions.description: Specimens received late in the week wait for the Sunday night or Monday processing run.

exceptions.name: Slide defect or mislabel
exceptions.description: Caught at slide matching; the block is recut or the slide relabelled.

exceptions.name: Missing cassette or tissue
exceptions.description: Count mismatch at embedding; the charge technologist traces it.

exceptions.name: Decalcification
exceptions.description: Bone or calcified tissue needs one to three days in decalcifying solution.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from receipt in histology to slides delivered to the pathologist
benchmarks.population: Author's estimate for community biopsies processed overnight and cut Monday to Friday

evidence.note: Overnight processing adds a day (ucdavis_tat) and daily histology turnaround after processing is about 9 to 10 hours (epmc_lean); weekend holds create the tail. The company postings put grossing on night shifts and cutting on evening shifts, so slides from a specimen received in the evening reach the pathologist on the second morning or earlier.

benchmarks.population: One academic histopathology laboratory before and after Lean (Raab et al. 2008)

pain_points.description: Overnight batch processing and Monday-to-Friday cutting set a one-day floor and a weekend tail on every case.
Labelling errors arise at accessioning, block labelling and cutting and depend on manual label checks.

evidence.note: Second identifiers were on only 75.7% of slides and 40% of blocks in the Q-Probes study.

pain_points.description: Embedding and microtomy are skilled manual tasks; histotechnologist shortages and evening and night shift work slow the line.

evidence.note: Evening and overnight shifts are posted.

pain_points.description: Recuts for poor sections send cases back through cutting and staining.

evidence.note: Common practice; share is an estimate.

sources.title: Europe PMC record: Nakhleh et al. 2011, Mislabeling of cases, specimens, blocks, and slides (CAP study of 136 institutions)
sources.publisher: Europe PMC (abstract of Archives of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine)
sources.supports: Mislabelling per 1,000: 1.1 cases, 1.0 specimens, 1.7 blocks, 1.1 slides; errors arose 20.9% before accessioning, 12.4% at accessioning, 21.7% at block labelling, 10.2% at grossing and 30.4% at tissue cutting; most were caught in the next one or two steps and 96.7% were corrected before the report was issued.

sources.title: Europe PMC records: Lean and processing studies in histology (Raab et al. 2008; Condel et al. 2004; Leong 1991)
sources.supports: Raab 2008: mean daily histopathology turnaround 9.7 hours falling to 9.0 hours after Lean, productivity 3,439 to 4,074 work units per FTE a month; Condel 2004: one-by-one continuous flow reduced cutting and labelling errors compared with batch work; Leong 1991: microwave short processing cycles of about 3 hours against an overnight cycle.

sources.title: Specimen turnaround time
sources.publisher: UC Davis Health, Department of Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
sources.supports: Biopsies 2 to 3 working days from accession; special stains and immunohistochemistry add 1 to 2 days; decalcification 1 to 2 days; intradepartmental consultation 1 to 2 days; overnight fixation 1 day; resubmission of tissue 1 to 2 days; recuts or deeper sections 1 to 2 days.

sources.title: Europe PMC records: surgical pathology turnaround studies (Volmar et al. 2015; Alshieban and Al-Surimi 2015; Patel et al. 2012; Novis et al. 1998)
sources.supports: Novis 1998: 85.9% of 5,384 biopsy diagnoses signed out by the second working day in 157 small hospitals; Patel 2012: 77% of non-biopsy cases within 2 days, with consultation, immunohistochemistry, malignancy and number of slides lengthening turnaround; Alshieban 2015: about 24% of routine cases missed the 2-day standard, delays at slide delivery, slide review, transcription editing and pathologist verification; Volmar 2015: median 2.72 days for large or complex specimens.

sources.title: Bringing down defects in surgical pathology reports (Paxton)
sources.supports: Q-Probes study of 73 institutions and 360,218 cases: 4.7 report defects (corrected reports) per 1,000, median 5.7; earlier studies 1.4 to 4.8 per 1,000; misinterpretation 14.6%, misidentification 13.3%, specimen defects 13.7%, other nondiagnostic defects 58.4%; 24.9% found by reviewing report text after sign-out; second identifiers on 75.7% of slides and 40% of blocks; laboratories where another pathologist reviews all malignancies before sign-out had fewer misidentifications.

assumptions: Case mix is mostly office biopsies of one to three blocks; about 0.5% need decalcification. Average hands-on minutes reflect about two blocks and two to four slides a case.
About 60% of cases are grossed by pathologists' assistants and 40% (small biopsies) by histotechnologists, as the company postings say both roles gross.
The company postings (2025 and 2026, after the reference period) show histology work on evening and night shifts; the same pattern is assumed for 2019-2022.
Processing runs, staining and the weekend hold are waiting with no hands-on time. Cases received Friday or Saturday (about 18%) wait for the Sunday night or Monday run.
Levels, special stains and recuts ordered by the pathologist after review are counted in the pathology sign-out workflow, not here.

The organisation file gives pathologists' assistants a loaded cost of CAD 55 to 75 an hour; the company's 2026 Pathology Assistant posting pays $28.00 to $30.50 an hour (about CAD 38 to 41 loaded). The organisation file cost is used, which may overstate grossing cost.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (hourly wage times 1.35).
